gloss: mouth; speech, word; command; opening; edge (of a sword); share; according to
summary: פֶּה is the mouth, which eats and kisses (Gen 8:11; 1Ki 19:18) and above all speaks: what comes out of a man’s mouth is his word, and what comes out of Yahweh’s mouth is his word, by which man lives (Deu 8:3) and which the prophets speak because he puts it in their mouths (Deu 18:18; Jer 1:9). So עַל־פִּי יַהְוֶה is “at Yahweh’s command”: Israel set out and camped by it (Num 9:18; 10:13), and to rebel against his mouth is to disobey him (Num 20:24). By likeness the mouth is any opening (of a well, a sack, a cave, the earth, the grave), the edge of a sword that “eats” (לְפִי־חֶרֶב), a share (פִּי שְׁנַיִם, “two shares”, Deu 21:17), and, with prepositions, “according to” (לְפִי, כְּפִי). The Aramaic פֻּם and the Peshitta’s pūmā are the same word, and it is mouth in every Semitic language.

words.gloss: mouth; speech, word; command; opening; edge; share; (with prepositions) according to
words.summary: About 500 uses, nearly always in the construct פִּי (“mouth of”) or with a suffix. The mouth itself; the mouth as what speaks, and so a person’s word and a ruler’s command; any opening; the edge of a sword; a share; and in לְפִי, כְּפִי and עַל־פִּי a preposition, “according to”. The corpus also files here the place name Pi-hahiroth (Exo 14:2, 9; Num 33:7), the reduplicated plural פִּיפִיּוֹת and the פִּים of 1Sa 13:21 (both below).

senses.definition: The mouth as part of the body: what eats and drinks, kisses, holds, and, of a beast, seizes its prey.

evidence.note: “Who has made a פֶּה for man? Or who makes the mute or the deaf, the seeing or the blind? Is it not I, Yahweh?”
The dove came back with a plucked olive leaf בְּפִיהָ, in her mouth.
Seven thousand, every knee that has not bowed to Baal “and every פֶּה that has not kissed him”.
“Meat and wine did not come into my mouth”: eating.
Those who lapped, putting their hand to their mouth.
David rescued the lamb “from its mouth”, the lion’s or the bear’s.
As the shepherd rescues from the lion’s mouth two legs or a piece of an ear.
“They open their mouth wide against me, a ravening and roaring lion.”
Elisha lay on the child, “his mouth on his mouth”.
“Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth.”
“All the labour of man is for his mouth, and yet the appetite is not filled.”
First-ripe figs that fall, when shaken, “into the mouth of the eater”.

senses.gloss: mouth as what speaks; speech, word, testimony
senses.definition: The mouth as the organ of speech, and so what a person says: his words, his testimony, his promise. Set beside the lips, the tongue and the heart. Of God, what goes out of his mouth is his word, which does what he sends it to do.

evidence.note: Moses: “I am heavy of פֶּה and heavy of tongue.”
“I will be with your mouth and teach you what you shall say.”
“You shall speak to him and put the words in his mouth, and I will be with your mouth and with his mouth.”
Aaron “shall be to you for a mouth (לְפֶה), and you shall be to him for God”: the mouth is the spokesman.
“פֶּה אֶל־פֶּה I speak with him”: Moses hears Yahweh directly, not in riddles.
“It is my mouth that speaks to you.”
“We will call the girl and ask her mouth”: ask her own word.
Yahweh opened the mouth of the donkey, and she spoke.
A man who vows “shall do according to all that goes out of his mouth”: his spoken word binds him.
“Man does not live by bread alone, but by all that goes out of the mouth of Yahweh”; quoted in Mat 4:4.
“I will put my words in his mouth, and he shall speak to them all that I command him.”
“The word is very near you, in your mouth and in your heart, to do it”; expounded in Rom 10:8–10.
Yahweh touched Jeremiah’s mouth: “I have put my words in your mouth.”
The coal touched the prophet’s mouth: “this has touched your lips”.
“For the mouth of Yahweh has spoken.”
“So shall my word be that goes out of my mouth: it shall not return to me empty.”
“By the word of Yahweh the heavens were made, and all their host by the breath of his mouth.”
“This book of the law shall not depart out of your mouth”: spoken and meditated.
“Let the words of my mouth and the meditation of my heart be acceptable before you.”
“From the fruit of a man’s mouth his belly is satisfied.”
The idols “have a mouth, but they do not speak”.
The servant “did not open his mouth”; quoted in Act 8:32.
“Nor was any deceit in his mouth”; quoted in 1Pe 2:22.
“At the mouth of two or three witnesses” the one worthy of death shall die, “not at the mouth of one witness”: the mouth is testimony.
“At the mouth of two witnesses or at the mouth of three witnesses a matter shall stand”; quoted in Mat 18:16 and 2Co 13:1.
The murderer is put to death “at the mouth of witnesses”.
Baruch wrote “from the mouth of Jeremiah”: at his dictation.
“To fulfil the word of Yahweh by the mouth of Jeremiah.”

senses.definition: What a ruler or God says as an order. עַל־פִּי is “at the command of”; to rebel against, or transgress, someone’s mouth is to disobey his command.

evidence.note: “עַל־פִּי יַהְוֶה the sons of Israel set out, and עַל־פִּי יַהְוֶה they camped”, as long as the cloud rested on the tabernacle.
“They kept the charge of Yahweh עַל־פִּי יַהְוֶה בְּיַד־מֹשֶׁה”: Yahweh’s command, given through Moses.
“They set out for the first time עַל־פִּי יַהְוֶה בְּיַד־מֹשֶׁה”, from Sinai in the order of the camps.
Pharaoh to Joseph: “וְעַל־פִּיךָ shall all my people be ruled (or kiss)”: under your command.
Joseph gave them wagons “עַל־פִּי פַרְעֹה”, as Pharaoh ordered.
They moved from the wilderness of Sin by their stages “at the mouth of Yahweh”.
Moses numbered the Levites “at the mouth of Yahweh, as he was commanded”.
“At his mouth they shall go out and at his mouth they shall come in”: at the priest’s word, after he asks Yahweh by the Urim.
Moses wrote their departures “at the mouth of Yahweh”.
Moses died there in Moab “at the mouth of Yahweh”.
“Why do you transgress (עֹבְרִים) the mouth of Yahweh?”, when they went up against his word.
Aaron shall not enter the land “because you rebelled against my mouth (מְרִיתֶם אֶת־פִּי) at the waters of Meribah”.
“You would not go up, and you rebelled against the mouth of Yahweh your God.”
“If you fear Yahweh … and do not rebel against the mouth of Yahweh.”
Saul: “I have sinned, for I have transgressed the mouth of Yahweh and your words.”
“Yahweh is righteous, for I have rebelled against his mouth.”
“Keep the king’s mouth”: his command.
Jehoiakim taxed the land to give the silver “at the mouth of Pharaoh”.
Caleb was given his portion “at the mouth of Yahweh to Joshua”.

senses.definition: By likeness, the opening of anything that can take in or let out: a well, a sack, a cave, a garment’s neck, a vessel, the earth, the grave. פֶּה לָפֶה, “mouth to mouth”, is from one end to the other.

evidence.note: A great stone was “on the mouth of the well”.
Jacob rolled the stone from the mouth of the well.
His silver was “in the mouth of his sack”.
“Roll great stones to the mouth of the cave.”
The robe of the ephod: “the mouth of its head” in the middle, with a binding round “its mouth”, “like the mouth of a coat of mail”: the neck opening.
The oil runs down on Aaron’s beard, “on the mouth (collar) of his garments”.
“It binds me like the mouth (collar) of my tunic.”
The mouth of the stand for the laver, round, a cubit and a half.
He threw the lead weight on the mouth of the ephah.
“The ground, which opened its mouth to receive your brother’s blood from your hand.”
“If the ground opens its mouth and swallows them, and they go down alive to the grave (שְׁאֹלָה).”
“The grave (שְׁאוֹל) has enlarged its appetite and opened its mouth beyond measure.”
“Our bones are scattered at the mouth of the grave.”
“Let not the pit close its mouth on me.”
Wisdom cries “beside the gates, at the mouth of the town”: its entrance.
The house of Baal was filled “פֶּה לָפֶה”, from end to end.
Manasseh filled Jerusalem with innocent blood “from end to end”.
The peoples filled the land with uncleanness “מִפֶּה אֶל־פֶּה”.

senses.definition: The edge of the sword, as the mouth with which it devours. לְפִי־חֶרֶב, “by the mouth of the sword”, is to kill with the sword; a sword of two mouths (פִּיּוֹת) is two-edged.

evidence.note: They killed Hamor and Shechem “לְפִי־חָרֶב”.
Joshua defeated Amalek “by the mouth of the sword”.
Devote the city and its cattle “by the mouth of the sword”.
The Sabeans struck the servants “by the mouth of the sword”.
“My sword shall devour (תֹּאכַל) flesh”: the sword eats, and so has a mouth.
“Shall the sword devour forever?”
Ehud made a sword “and it had two פֵיוֹת”: two edges.
The strange woman’s end is “sharp as a sword of פִּיּוֹת”: two-edged.
“He made my mouth like a sharp sword”: the servant’s mouth and the sword’s edge brought together.
“They shall fall by the mouth of the sword” (στόματι μαχαίρης; Peshitta בּפֻומָא דּחַרבָּא): the Hebrew idiom in the New Testament.
They “escaped the mouth of the sword”.

senses.definition: A share, as a mouthful is: פִּי שְׁנַיִם, “a mouth of two”, is two shares, the firstborn’s double portion; set against “the third” it is two parts of three.

evidence.note: The father shall acknowledge the firstborn “by giving him פִּי שְׁנַיִם of all that he has, for he is the beginning of his strength; the right of the firstborn is his”.
Elisha asks: “Let there be פִּי־שְׁנַיִם of your spirit upon me”: the firstborn’s share.
“In all the land פִּי־שְׁנַיִם in it shall be cut off and die, but the third shall be left in it”: two parts of three.

senses.gloss: (לְפִי, כְּפִי, עַל־פִּי) according to, in proportion to
senses.definition: With prepositions, “at the mouth of” becomes a preposition: according to, in proportion to, as much as; with אֲשֶׁר, inasmuch as.

evidence.note: The Passover lamb counted “each according to his eating (לְפִי אָכְלוֹ)”.
The manna: “each gathered according to his eating”.
Joseph fed his father’s house with bread “according to the little ones”: by the number in each house.
“לְפִי the many years you shall increase its price, and לְפִי the few years you shall diminish it”: in proportion.
The priest values him “עַל־פִּי what the hand of the one who vows can reach”.
The wagons given to the Levites “each according to his service (כְּפִי עֲבֹדָתוֹ)”.
“עַל־פִּי the lot his inheritance shall be divided.”
Each tribe gives cities to the Levites “according to its inheritance”.
“וּלְפִי the lifting of the cloud”: whenever it lifted, they set out.
“Train up a child עַל־פִּי his way.”
“A man is praised according to his understanding.”
“Reap according to steadfast love.”
“כְּפִי אֲשֶׁר you do not keep my ways”: inasmuch as.
“We told him עַל־פִּי these words”: in answer to his questions.

evidence.locator: Deu.8.3, פִי → στόματος; Gen.34.26, לְפִי־חֶרֶב → ἐν στόματι μαχαίρας; στόμα renders פֶּה ×282

evidence.note: Deu 8:3 quoted: “by every word that proceeds out of the στόματος of God”.
Deu 19:15: “that ἐπὶ στόματος two or three witnesses every word may be established”.
Deu 30:14: “the word is near you, in your στόματι and in your heart”.
Isa 53:7: “so he opened not his στόμα”.
Isa 53:9: “nor was deceit found in his στόματι”.
Psa 78:2: “I will open my στόμα in parables”.
Isa 29:13: “this people draws near to me with their στόματι”.
Psa 8:3: “out of the στόματος of babes and sucklings”.
Psa 10:7: “whose στόμα is full of cursing and bitterness”.
Isa 11:4: the lawless one consumed “with the spirit of his στόματος”.
“They shall fall by the στόματι of the sword”: לְפִי־חֶרֶב.

evidence.locator: Jdg.3.16, שְׁנֵי פֵיוֹת → δίστομος; Pro.5.4, חֶרֶב פִּיּוֹת → διστόμου; Psa.149.6, פִּיפִיּוֹת → δίστομος

evidence.note: The word of God is “sharper than any two-edged (δίστομον) sword”; the Peshitta, “a sword of two mouths” (דַּתֿרֵין פֻּומֵיה).
“Out of his mouth went a sharp two-edged (δίστομος) sword.”

evidence.locator: Num.14.41, פִּי יַהְוֶה → τὸ ῥῆμα κυρίου; Exo.17.1, Deu.1.26, Deu.34.5 the same; ῥῆμα renders פֶּה ×12

evidence.note: “By every ῥήματι that proceeds out of the mouth of God”: the word that is the mouth’s.

parallels.note: The lips, beside the mouth as what speaks.
The heart beside the mouth: what is said and what is meant.
Yahweh “spoke with his mouth … and with his hand has fulfilled it”: word and deed.

opposites.note: Near with the mouth, far in the heart: words without the heart behind them.

phrases.gloss: for the mouth of Yahweh has spoken
put a word in someone’s mouth: give them what to say
mouth to mouth: face to face, directly

evidence.note: “His mouth shall speak with his mouth, and his eyes shall see his eyes.”

phrases.gloss: open the mouth: begin to speak

evidence.note: Its opposite: “I was mute, I did not open my mouth.”

phrases.gloss: open the mouth wide: to swallow or devour

evidence.note: “I lay my hand on my mouth.”

phrases.gloss: by the mouth (edge) of the sword
two shares: the firstborn’s portion; two parts of three

words.summary: Twice, a plural of פֶּה with its first syllable doubled, used where פִּיּוֹת would be: the edges of a blade. Its two tokens are counted under פֶּה, with which the corpus files them.

senses.gloss: edges (of a sword, a threshing sledge)
senses.definition: The cutting edges of a blade: a sword of פִּיפִיּוֹת is two-edged, as a sword of פִּיּוֹת is; a threshing sledge “possessing פִּיפִיּוֹת” is one set with sharp edges.

evidence.note: “The high praises of God in their throat, and a sword of פִּיפִיּוֹת in their hand.”
“I have made you a new sharp threshing sledge, בַּעַל פִּיפִיּוֹת; you shall thresh the mountains.”

words.summary: Once, as the charge for sharpening tools when the Philistines kept smiths out of Israel. The verse shows a payment and no more; scripture does not give its value, and how the word comes from פֶּה is not shown. The corpus files its one token under פֶּה; if it is “mouths”, shares, it might be a fraction of the shekel, as פִּי שְׁנַיִם is two shares of three (Zec 13:8), but that is not evident from the text.

senses.definition: A charge paid for sharpening ploughshares, mattocks, axes and goads.

evidence.note: “And the charge was a פִים for the ploughshares and the mattocks, … and for the axes, and for setting the goads.”
All Israel went down to the Philistines to sharpen their tools.

words.summary: Six times in Daniel, the Aramaic of פֶּה with an m: the mouth that speaks and eats, and the mouth of the lions’ den.

senses.definition: The mouth of man or beast, as what speaks and what devours.

evidence.note: “While the word was still in the king’s mouth, a voice fell from heaven.”
The bear had three ribs “in its mouth between its teeth”; cf. Rev 13:2.
The little horn had eyes like a man’s “and a mouth speaking great things”; cf. Rev 13:5.
“My God sent his angel and shut the lions’ mouth”; cf. Heb 11:33.

senses.definition: The opening of the pit into which Daniel was cast.

evidence.note: A stone was brought and laid “on the mouth of the den”, and the king sealed it.

evidence.locator: Dan.7.5, בְּפֻמַּהּ → ἐν τῷ στόματι αὐτῆς; Dan.7.8, וּפֻם → στόμα; στόμα renders פֻּם ×4

evidence.note: The beast was given “a στόμα speaking great things and blasphemies”: Dan 7:8.
Its mouth “as the mouth of a lion”, beside the bear of Dan 7:5.
Those who by faith “stopped the mouths (στόματα) of lions”: Dan 6:23.

words.summary: The Peshitta’s ܦܘܡܐ (pūmā), 86 times in the New Testament, for στόμα, including where the New Testament quotes the Hebrew פֶּה, and with the Hebrew’s own idioms: the mouth of the sword, a sword of two mouths, the mouth of the prophets.

senses.definition: The mouth, and what goes out of it, as the Hebrew פֶּה.

evidence.note: “By every word that goes out of the mouth (ܦܘܡܗ) of God”: Deu 8:3.
“At the mouth of two or three witnesses”: Deu 19:15.
“As he spoke by the mouth of his holy prophets.”
Dan 7:8.

senses.definition: The sword’s edge, as in the Hebrew לְפִי־חֶרֶב.

evidence.note: “They shall fall by the mouth of the sword (בּפֻומָא דּחַרבָּא).”
“They escaped from the mouth of the sword.”
“Sharper than a sword of two mouths (דַּתֿרֵין פֻּומֵיה).”

cognates.gloss: mouth; the mouth (opening) of a river, valley, street or road; (فَاهَ بِهِ) he uttered it
cognates.note: Lane gives فَمٌ as originally فَوَهٌ, with the plural أَفْوَاهٌ, and the verb فَاهَ “to utter”: the mouth as what speaks. فُوَّهَةٌ is the mouth of a river, a valley or a road, “likened to the mouth properly so called as being the first place of ingress”: the Hebrew’s opening.

evidence.note: “The mouth … it is originally فَوَهٌ … when you form the dim. or the pl., you restore it to its original state, saying فُوَيْهٌ and أَفْوَاهٌ.”
فُوهٌ, فَاهٌ, فِيهٌ, فُوَّهَةٌ and فَمٌ “all signify the same, i.e. the mouth”; فَاهَ بِهِ “he uttered it, or pronounced it”.
“The mouth of a place … of a river, or rivulet, and of a valley, or water-course … and of a street, and of a road.”

cognates.gloss: mouth; word, speech, command; opening; (ana pî) in accordance with
cognates.note: Akkadian pû has the Hebrew’s whole range: the mouth, the word and command, an opening and the source of a watercourse, and in ana pî “in accordance with”, the Hebrew לְפִי.

evidence.note: accordance; command; entrance; in proportion to; mouth; opening; order; source of watercourse; speech; tip; utterance; word.

evidence.locator: tsae x000080010, ana pî [with respect to] PRP
evidence.note: in accordance with.

cognates.note: In the Baal texts, “the word did not go out of her mouth (bph)”: the mouth that speaks.

evidence.note: py 1.6:I:22; ph 1.2:IV:6 “mouth” (H. pê, Akkad. pû, Arab. fū, fī, fā; cf. Aram. pum).

cognates.gloss: mouth; permission, authorization; (lpy) in accordance with, because of
cognates.note: The Punic “without my py” is “without my permission”, as the Hebrew עַל־פִּי is “at the command of”; and lpy is the Hebrew לְפִי, “in accordance with”.

evidence.note: “n.m. 1. MOUTH” (KAI 11, Byblos, a muzzle “on my mouth”); “2. PERMISSION, AUTHORIZATION” (KAI 79.6/11, “without my permission”).
“prep. 1. IN ACCORDANCE WITH” (KAI 69.18, “in accordance with the document”); “2. BECAUSE OF, BY REASON OF”.

cognates.note: The Targums’ word for פֶּה, the mouth of a man and of a well, and like the Hebrew לְפִי, כְּפִי, a preposition “according to”; its plural פּוּמִין renders the “two-edged” sword of Pro 5:4.

evidence.note: “= h. פֶּה. Targ. Ex. IV, 11 … Targ. O. Gen. XXIX, 2 … כְּפוּם, לְפוּם = h. כְּפִי, לְפִי, according to. Targ. Lev. XXV, 52 … Pl. פּוּמִין … Targ. Prov. V, 4.”
The Syriac pūmā of the Peshitta.

cognates.gloss: mouth; orifice, entrance; cutting edge of a sword
cognates.note: The Ge'ez mouth is also the sword’s edge, as in the Hebrew לְפִי־חֶרֶב; the Tigre and Amharic words keep the same senses.

evidence.note: “mouth”; “orifice, entrance”; “cutting edge of a sword”; from Proto-Semitic *pay-.

doctrine.statement: What goes out of Yahweh’s mouth is his word: the heavens were made “by the word of Yahweh, and all their host by the breath of his mouth” (Psa 33:6, 9), and that word “shall not return to me empty, but shall accomplish what I please” (Isa 55:11). Israel was humbled in the wilderness and fed with manna to learn “that man does not live by bread alone, but by all that goes out of the mouth of Yahweh” (Deu 8:3), and Jesus answered the adversary with that verse (Mat 4:4). From the verses: the word that comes from God’s mouth is what makes and what gives life, and to live is to live by it.

Yahweh made the mouth (Exo 4:11) and gave his prophets what to say by putting his words in their mouths: to Moses, “I will be with your mouth” (Exo 4:12); to Balaam, “the word God puts in my mouth, that I will speak” (Num 22:38); to Jeremiah, “I have put my words in your mouth” (Jer 1:9). Aaron was to be Moses’ “mouth”, and Moses “as God” to him (Exo 4:16): a prophet is the mouth of the one who sends him. So what the prophets said is called the word of Yahweh “by the mouth of Jeremiah” (2Ch 36:21; Ezr 1:1), and “the mouth of Yahweh has spoken” (Isa 1:20; 40:5). The prophet like Moses would have Yahweh’s words in his mouth and speak all that he commanded (Deu 18:18); Peter says that prophet is Jesus (Act 3:22–23), who said, “I have not spoken of myself, but the Father who sent me gave me a commandment what I should say” (Jhn 12:49). From the verses: scripture’s prophecy is God’s own word in a man’s mouth, and Jesus spoke the Father’s words, not his own.

Israel set out and camped “at the mouth of Yahweh”, staying while the cloud rested and moving when it lifted (Num 9:18–23), and so left Sinai (Num 10:13). Going against it is called rebelling against his mouth: at Meribah, for which Moses and Aaron did not enter the land (Num 20:24; 27:14), and at Kadesh, when the people would not go up and then went up without him (Deu 1:26, 43). Saul confessed, “I have transgressed the mouth of Yahweh” (1Sa 15:24). From the verses: what Yahweh says is to be done as he says it, when he says it; obedience is not a matter of the people’s own judgment of the moment.

The law put no one to death “at the mouth of one witness”, but “at the mouth of two or three witnesses” (Deu 17:6; 19:15; Num 35:30). Jesus applied it to a brother who sins and will not hear (Mat 18:16), Paul to his own dealings with Corinth and to charges against an elder (2Co 13:1; 1Ti 5:19), and Hebrews to the one who despised Moses’ law (Heb 10:28). From the verses: a charge stands on the agreeing word of more than one witness, in the ecclesia as in Israel.

The servant of Isaiah was led like a lamb to the slaughter and “did not open his mouth”, and “there was no deceit in his mouth” (Isa 53:7, 9); Philip and Peter say this is Jesus (Act 8:32–35; 1Pe 2:22–23). Yet his mouth is also his weapon: “he made my mouth like a sharp sword” (Isa 49:2), and the branch from Jesse “shall strike the earth with the rod of his mouth, and with the breath of his lips he shall kill the wicked” (Isa 11:4). Paul says the Lord will consume the lawless one “with the spirit of his mouth” at his coming (2Th 2:8), and John saw the sharp sword going out of his mouth, with which he strikes the nations (Rev 1:16; 19:15). From the verses: the one who was silent before his accusers will judge by his word when he returns.

Moses said the word was not far off but “in your mouth and in your heart, to do it” (Deu 30:14); Paul reads it of the word of faith: “if you confess with your mouth the Lord Jesus and believe in your heart that God raised him from the dead, you will be saved” (Rom 10:8–10). Isaiah condemned a people who drew near “with their mouth” while their heart was far from Yahweh (Isa 29:13), and Jesus applied it to the Pharisees (Mat 15:7–9). From the verses: the mouth and the heart are to agree; confession without belief, or worship of the lips only, is not what God accepts.

note: Drafted 2026-11-13 for Numbers 10 (עַל־פִּי יַהְוֶה, Num 10:13); the word does not occur in Leviticus 23. Root key: the corpus files פֶּה (q.al.aa) and its Aramaic פֻּם (xq.ac.ac, under פמ) with no shared root; q.al.aa has an empty root, so the entry takes the noun’s own consonants פה as the README directs, and lexicon-brief פה finds no words. The q.al.aa tokens (505) include the place Pi-hahiroth (Exo 14:2, 9; Num 33:7), not a person and so no name entry; פִּיפִיּוֹת (Isa 41:15; Psa 149:6), whose own key q.bi.ae (a cross-reference filed under פימ) has no tokens; and פִּים of 1Sa 13:21, which has no key of its own (q.bi.aa is BDB’s root heading פים/פאם). Left out: פֹּה “here” (q.am.aa, 82 tokens; also פֹּא q.aa.ab, פּוֹ), the same consonants but an adverb with its own cognates (Ugaritic p “here”, Segert p. 197; Phoenician) and no tie to the mouth: a homograph entry of its own. Left out also פִּימָה “fat” (Job 15:27, q.bi.ab) and פֵּאָה “corner, side” (q.ab.ab), which BDB puts under other roots; whether either goes back to פה is not shown. Leads not followed: Akkadian šinipu “two-thirds” (Oracc armep x000018890) beside פִּי שְׁנַיִם “two parts” (Zec 13:8); and the Judean weights inscribed pym, which would give פִּים a value of about two-thirds of a shekel (archaeological, not in sources.json). Not consulted: Leslau and Dillmann for Ge'ez (Wiktionary only), DULAT for Ugaritic, Payne Smith for the Syriac (SEDRA used). Peshitta: SEDRA lexeme 2465 ܦܘܡܐ, 86 tokens in 80 verses, found through the Peshitta text. Open questions: (1) whether פִּים belongs here; (2) the ‘share’ sense rests on the three פִּי שְׁנַיִם verses; (3) the doctrine notes.
